name: Zürich
fact: Legend says Charlemagne founded the twin-towered Grossmünster, the city's most famous landmark.

name: Rhine Falls
fact: One of Europe's most powerful waterfalls — the Rhine thunders 23 m down near Schaffhausen.

name: Appenzell
fact: Home of Appenzeller cheese, washed in a secret herbal brine whose recipe is still a closely kept secret.

name: St. Moritz
fact: This alpine resort hosted the Winter Olympics twice, in 1928 and 1948.

name: Lugano
fact: Palm trees in Switzerland! Lugano sits in Italian-speaking Ticino, on a sunny lake.

name: Château de Chillon
fact: A castle on the water of Lake Geneva that inspired Lord Byron's poem "The Prisoner of Chillon".

name: Geneva
fact: The Jet d'Eau shoots water about 140 m into the air over Lake Geneva.

name: Bern
fact: The Zytglogge clock tower has marked time for the Swiss capital since medieval times; its astronomical clock dates from 1530.

name: Lucerne
fact: The Chapel Bridge (Kapellbrücke), from the 14th century, is one of Europe's oldest covered wooden bridges.

name: Matterhorn
fact: 4,478 m of pure Swiss icon — and where our edelweiss grows. You made it: enjoy 15% off!
